UPPER BOUND ON runtime:expression-statement — 266 scripts ⭐ a STRICT upper bound: every line this guard refuses is DELETED, which is more permissive than any correct implementation can be.
scripts it refuses at all : 2 build BEFORE : 20 build AFTER (perfect, at best) : 20 GAIN, AT BEST : 0
⛔ ZERO. Solving this guard perfectly moves the build count by nothing ON THE FIRST-BLOCKER PATH. A guard whose refused lines are BINDINGS can still gain: deleting a binding breaks its consumers, so the peel is stricter than an implementation. Measured once, +1 forecast -> +2 real. That is not a reason to skip it — it may still be a correctness fix — but it IS a reason not to expect movement, and to say so up front.

testcase.name: terminal-reachable stylesheets — text contrast in every theme > every baseline entry carries a reason
terminal-reachable stylesheets — text contrast in every theme > CONTROL: the text check SEES --loss/--gain as text (plain and with a fallback) and ignores fills/borders
terminal-reachable stylesheets — text contrast in every theme > CONTROL: the contrast audit SEES a failing rule and records an unreadable one instead of throwing
CORR windows > every window the lookback arg accepts is a window the panel draws
CORR windows > 2Y is the last 504 shared returns, equal to the independent reference
CORR windows > YTD is every return dated in the newest year, equal to the independent reference
CORR windows > the panel opens on 2Y / YTD when typed, and its matrix shows those numbers
CORR windows > a window it cannot draw is said out loud, never silently replaced
familyRows > lists long then short, upper-cased, with a side
EtfPanel > a stock: its leveraged and inverse ETFs, and an honest note about the reverse lookup
EtfPanel > an ETF: its holdings, top weights first, the rest counted
EtfPanel > a stock with no single-stock leveraged ETFs says so, naming the scope
EtfPanel > a leveraged ETF names its underlying and marks itself
EtfPanel > a 402 on the family is a plan note; the holdings still render
EtfPanel > a known ETF with no holdings is an error with Retry, never "holds nothing"
EtfPanel > both reads failing is one error with Retry
EtfPanel > with no ticker it asks for one and fetches nothing
ETF in the registry > NVDA ETF opens the Etf panel
HELP Advanced disclosure > folds rules, keys and addresses under a closed "Advanced" disclosure
HELP Advanced disclosure > keeps "Start here" and the function list outside it, and before it
HELP Advanced disclosure > opens when its summary is activated
HELP Advanced disclosure > HELP <code> shows no Advanced section
MOST MINE > lists only the member's names when MINE is on
MOST MINE > without MINE every mover is listed and the chip is off (and my-sets is never read)
MOST MINE > the chip writes MINE into this panel's command, keeping the lens
MOST MINE > none of yours moving says so, and how "your names" is built
MOST > lists every mover with last, % change, volume and volume vs average, and subscribes them live
MOST > lenses, sort and the price / volume floors change what is listed
MOST > the lens a member typed (MOST DOWN) is the one it opens on
MOST > a row click LOADS the name into the linked group (keepFunction), and row numbers publish the same
MOST > the why link opens the catalyst board's story inline, and offers MOVE for the full one
MOST > outside the regular session it never says Live, and names the basis it is showing
MOST > after hours adds the after-hours column; the regular session does not show it
MOST > a failed movers read is an error with a retry, not an empty tape; a 402 is a plan, not an outage
MOST > a failed side source is NAMED and the list still renders from the rest
MOST > an empty tape says so in words, and an over-tight filter says what to loosen
MOST > shows the loading skeleton while the first read is in flight
MOST > TERM-047: MOST RVOL shows the volume scan's own four-count receipt when it is served, and nothing while dark

testcase.name: 9. on a phone the screen picker opens as a bottom sheet with its name and search box
9b. on a tablet the screen picker stays the anchored popover
head of base_render, +N stripped, said plainly with the textbook name in the tooltip
null base: neutral wording, because the payload cannot say WHY the columns are empty
zero volume says so and is quiet
pivot detail only with a finite pivot and price
pivot detail rides the row when base_pivot_px exists
leading whitespace before a parenthetical keeps the render instead of going blank
pivot under 10 keeps two decimals
active structures come from the answered filters and the library labels, found by key
B2: the matched structure leads and the render head follows as "also"
B2: a head that already is the matched structure reads as before, pivot kept
B2: with no structure filter the head leads as before
B2: zero volume and missing history stay quiet even under a structure screen
plain words: jargon structure names are spelled out, the textbook name stays in the tooltip
structure labels are the library presets, never the "Any" row or another filter
B2 against the REAL meta shape (no column field): the structure is found and the head is whole
a price far past the pivot says "extended", never a big percentage
a stale pivot is dated, not measured against today
stale means MORE than two closed sessions behind the row bars_asof
the setup line dates a stale pivot and measures a fresh one
zero volume names the session it describes; "today" only when bars_asof is today
the pivot line is titled for the head structure in plain words, and hidden when stale
the head tooltip is its library description, led by the textbook name when renamed
trend shapes read as trend descriptions, not setups
every plain structure name keys a REAL library label (a typo would never match)
defaults to the first list and adds to it
remembers the chosen list
curated lists are never offered as a target
B15: with no watchlist, W creates "Screener picks", adds the stock, says so, and re-reads the lists
B15: never creates when the member already has a list (the cache was just stale)
B15: a failed confirming read creates nothing (an empty cache may be a swallowed error)
B15: a member whose only lists are linked gets a message, never a new list
B15: two quick presses create ONE list
B15: a refused create says so and adds nothing
a refused add says so
a stored id that no longer exists falls back to the first list
linked lists are not offered as a target
adding while the lists are still loading says so
a failed load is not reported as having no lists

def _busy_answer(fn) -> Any: \"\"\"`fn()`, with a database another writer holds past the timeout answered 503 `busy` (the house sentence, no-store) and nothing else changed: for the doors that keep their own refusal shapes outside `_w11` (review m-4: POST and DELETE /{id}/helpful). `_w11` answers busy itself, by the same `_database_busy` test.\"\"\" try: return fn() except sqlite3.OperationalError as e: if not _database_busy(e): raise raise _err(503, \"busy\", DATABASE_BUSY_SENTENCE) from None
def _w11(fn) -> Any: \"\"\"Run `fn()`; answer every refusal from its CLASS (W9-R14). None is the one 404. 11.20 R1: a database another writer holds past the timeout is 503 `busy` with the house sentence, never a 500; the client resends the same Idempotency-Key on `busy`. A busy write rolled back; a Use is TWO transactions (its key reservation and adoption commit first, then the note), and a busy note create releases the Use's own reservation (at once, or in the background as soon as the lock clears), so the same-key retry makes the note (review m-1).\"\"\" try: out = fn() except HTTPException: raise except ToolError as e: # ShareError, LibraryError, CountCapError, KeyReused, RoutineError, TrackerError if e.status == 404: raise public.not_found() slot = getattr(e, \"slot\", None) raise _err(e.status, e.code, e.sentence, **({\"slot\": slot} if isinstance(slot, str) and slot else {})) except gallery.GalleryConflict as e: raise _err(409, getattr(e, \"code\", None) or \"conflict\", str(e)) except gallery.GalleryError as e: raise _err(400, \"invalid\", str(e)) except gallery.GalleryServerError as e: raise _err(500, \"server\", str(e)) except wdefs.WidgetError as e: # m-3: by STATUS only (W9-R14). The widget store's cap never reaches here as a WidgetError: every wave 11 # door that can make a widget wraps it in `CountCapError` (`template_gallery._cap_sentence`). if e.status == 404: raise public.not_found() raise _err(409 if e.status == 409 else 400, \"conflict\" if e.status == 409 else \"invalid\", e.sentence) except notes_service.NoteValidationError as e: # I-1: a Use's note fields, refused by the notes module raise _err(400, \"invalid\", str(e)) except notes_service.NoteConflictError: raise _err(409, \"conflict\", NOTE_CONFLICT_SENTENCE) except notes_service.NoteLockedError as e: raise _err(423, \"locked\", str(e)) except js.StyleNotFound: raise public.not_found() except js.StyleValidationError as e: raise _err(400, \"invalid\", str(e)) except PlanTooNew as e: raise _err(409, \"too_new\", e.sentence) except PlanError as e: raise _err(400, \"invalid\", e.sentence) except wrun.EngineBusy as e: raise _err(503, \"busy\", e.sentence) except wrun.EngineTooLong as e: raise _err(503, \"too_long\", e.sentence) except sqlite3.OperationalError as e: if not _database_busy(e): raise raise _err(503, \"busy\", DATABASE_BUSY_SENTENCE) from None if out is None: raise public.not_found() return out

# ── card facts (carry: `_summary` gains `contains` and the viewer's `credit`) ─────────────────────── # # `_summary` already carries `usedBy` (the distinct-use count; the client words 0 as \"New\") and `updatedAt`. _PARTS_SQL = ( \"SELECT g.id, '{part}', json_extract(p.value, '$.key'), json_extract(p.value, '$.name'),\" \" json_extract(p.value, '$.plan') FROM j2_template_gallery g, json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(g.payload_json)\" \" THEN g.payload_json ELSE '{{}}' END, '$.{part}') p WHERE g.id IN ({marks}) AND g.item_type = 'style'\" \" AND json_type(p.value) = 'object'\") _BLOCKS_SQL = ( \"SELECT g.id, p.value FROM j2_template_gallery g, json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(g.payload_json)\" \" THEN g.payload_json ELSE '{{}}' END, '$.blocks') p WHERE g.id IN ({marks}) AND g.item_type = 'style'\" \" AND json_valid(g.payload_json) AND json_extract(g.payload_json, '$.format') = 2\" \" AND json_type(p.value) = 'object' ORDER BY g.id, CAST(p.key AS INTEGER)\")
def _part_name(family: str, settings: dict, block: dict, parts: dict) -> str | None: from api.services.journal_two import slot_fill, template_tools, trackers if family == \"built\": ref = settings.get(\"ref\") if isinstance(settings.get(\"ref\"), str) else \"\" if ref.startswith(\"inline:\"): return (parts.get((\"definitions\", ref[len(\"inline:\"):])) or (None,))[0] if ref.startswith(\"shelf:\"): try: name, _reason = slot_fill.slot_name(block, {}) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 -- an unreadable shelf ref names nothing return None return name return None pool = \"routines\" if family == \"routine\" else \"trackers\" if isinstance(settings.get(\"inline\"), str): return (parts.get((pool, settings[\"inline\"])) or (None,))[0] templates = template_tools.ROUTINE_TEMPLATES if family == \"routine\" else template_tools.TRACKER_TEMPLATES if isinstance(settings.get(\"template\"), str) and settings[\"template\"] in templates: return templates[settings[\"template\"]].get(\"name\") ref = settings.get(\"ref\") if family == \"tracker\" and isinstance(ref, str) and ref in trackers.BUILTIN: return trackers.BUILTIN[ref].get(\"name\") return None

It is PINNED, not promised: both read tests/fixtures_plain_text.json (tests/test_plain_text_parity.py ⇄ lib/plainText.parity.test.js), and each rail fails on a leaf one side reads and the other does not.
The rules are textBetween's, verbatim, and the same ones the citation text uses (note_citation_text.flatten, with a newline where this has a space): · text runs inside one textblock join with NOTHING -- a mark (bold, highlight, link) is invisible, so \"**NV**DA\" reads \"NVDA\" and a highlighted phrase mid-sentence keeps single spaces around it; · every textblock (an EMPTY one included) is preceded by one separator, except the first thing in the document to earn one; · a container that is not a textblock (list, quote, table, toggle, ...) adds nothing of its own; · a BLOCK leaf is preceded by a separator only when it reads as text; an INLINE leaf never is. ⚰️ Until 2026-09-23 every text node was joined with a space, so a partly bold word was indexed as two words and a search for it missed the note.

# ── The \"used in\" projection (Notebook widgets phase 2, Task 8.9) ─────────── # A `builtWidget` embed (a saved widget placed in a note) names its widget by # `params.defId` and the revision it was placed at by `params.defRev`. Each one # adds a `j2_tool_uses` row `(user_id, note_id, \"widget\", defId, defRev)`, so a # saved widget can answer \"which notes use me\" (widget_definitions.used_in_notes). # The row is a fact about THIS note's body only: a defId that is not the note # owner's own widget still gets a row under the note owner's user_id, and the # reader's `user_id` join is what keeps it from counting for anyone else. # ⛔ ONE FACT IN TWO FILES: this is notebook_widgets.BUILT_KIND, restated rather # than imported because notebook_widgets imports far more than this module may. _BUILT_WIDGET_ID = \"builtWidget\" _TOOL_KIND_WIDGET = \"widget\" # Routines and trackers (Task 9.10) are `widgetEmbed` blocks too: widgetId `routine` names its # routine by `params.routineId`, widgetId `tracker` its tracker by `params.trackerId`. Each adds a # `j2_tool_uses` row `(user_id, note_id, \"routine\"|\"tracker\", id, NULL)` (no revision: a routine # is live, not placed at a revision), read by routines.used_in_notes / trackers.used_in_notes with # the same user_id join as above. # ⛔ ONE FACT IN TWO FILES: these are the widget ids `routine` and `tracker` in # app/src/widgets/registry.js, restated rather than imported because the registry is JavaScript. # tests/test_tool_uses_projection.py pins them against that file's text. _ROUTINE_ID = \"routine\" _TRACKER_ID = \"tracker\" _TOOL_PARAM_KEY = {_ROUTINE_ID: \"routineId\", _TRACKER_ID: \"trackerId\"} _SQLITE_INT_MIN, _SQLITE_INT_MAX = -(2 ** 63), 2 ** 63 - 1
def _tool_use_row(params: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str, int | None] | None: \"\"\"A `builtWidget` embed's (kind, tool_id, rev), or None when it names no widget. Never raises: a bad embed is skipped and the note still saves (the degrade rule of _sync_note_sidecars).\"\"\" def_id = params.get(\"defId\") if not isinstance(def_id, str) or not def_id: return None # Bound into the INSERT below: a value SQLite cannot encode (a lone UTF-16 surrogate, # an integer past 64 bits) would raise there and roll back the whole note write. try: def_id.encode(\"utf-8\") except UnicodeEncodeError: return None rev = params.get(\"defRev\") if isinstance(rev, bool) or not isinstance(rev, int) or not _SQLITE_INT_MIN <= rev <= _SQLITE_INT_MAX: rev = None return (_TOOL_KIND_WIDGET, def_id, rev)
def _routine_tracker_use_row(widget_id: str, params: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str, int | None] | None: \"\"\"A `routine` / `tracker` embed's (kind, tool_id, None), or None when it names none. Never raises, for the same reason as _tool_use_row.\"\"\" tool_id = params.get(_TOOL_PARAM_KEY[widget_id]) if not isinstance(tool_id, str) or not tool_id: return None try: tool_id.encode(\"utf-8\") except UnicodeEncodeError: return None return (widget_id, tool_id, None)
# ── An internal note link MARK (Plan A Task 2, L-2) ───────────────────────── # An imported wiki link resolves to a `link` mark whose href is # `/journal?j2tab=notebook&note=<id>` (note_connectors/convert/rewrite.py), not a # `noteLink` node, so it used to be invisible to backlinks and the graph. It is # projected into j2_note_links alongside the nodes. Only this exact shape counts: # the two params in either order, nothing else in the query, no fragment. # ⛔ ONE FACT IN TWO FILES: INTERNAL_NOTE_RE in # app/src/pages/journal-2-0/lib/linkClickOpen.js (what opens in-app) is this # pattern; test_note_links_internal_href.py reads that literal and pins the two. _INTERNAL_NOTE_RE = re.compile( r\"^/journal\\?(?:j2tab=notebook&note=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)|note=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)&j2tab=notebook)$\")
def _internal_note_id(href: Any) -> str | None: \"\"\"The note id an in-app note link names, or None for any other href.\"\"\" if not isinstance(href, str): return None m = _INTERNAL_NOTE_RE.fullmatch(href.strip()) return (m.group(1) or m.group(2)) if m else None
def _internal_link_href(text_node: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None: \"\"\"A TEXT node's link href when it is an internal note link, else None. The caller has already read the node's type (the one-walk rule: each node's type is read once, test_sync_note_sidecars_walks_the_document_exactly_once).\"\"\" marks = text_node.get(\"marks\") if not isinstance(marks, list): return None for mark in marks: if isinstance(mark, dict) and mark.get(\"type\") == \"link\": attrs = mark.get(\"attrs\") href = attrs.get(\"href\") if isinstance(attrs, dict) else None return href if _internal_note_id(href) else None return None
def _sync_note_sidecars( conn: sqlite3.Connection, user_id: str, note_id: str, body_json: dict[str, Any] | None, body_plain: str | None, ) -> None: \"\"\"Rebuild every note-content sidecar projection inside the caller's transaction (no commit here): the five below, plus j2_note_checkins (P2 Tier 3) and j2_tool_uses (Notebook widgets phase 2, Task 8.9), which ride the same walk. Replaces the old _sync_note_embeds / _sync_note_mentions / _sync_note_links / _sync_note_fact_refs / _sync_note_excerpt_refs quintet, which every call site invoked together in this exact order -- see the module comment above for why combining them is a real perf win and not just tidying.\"\"\" embeds: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] checkins: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] tool_uses: list[tuple[str, str, int | None]] = [] link_ids: list[str] = [] fact_ids: list[str] = [] excerpt_ids: list[str] = [] has_task = [False] # wave 10: whether the task index needs its own walk at all
def walk(node: Any) -> str | None: \"\"\"Visits `node`; returns its internal note link href when it is a text node carrying one (its PARENT decides whether that starts a new link).\"\"\" if not isinstance(node, dict): return None ntype = node.get(\"type\") if ntype == \"text\": return _internal_link_href(node) if ntype == \"taskItem\": has_task[0] = True if ntype == \"widgetEmbed\": attrs = node.get(\"attrs\") if not isinstance(attrs, dict): attrs = {} params = attrs.get(\"params\") if not isinstance(params, dict): params = {} widget_id = attrs.get(\"widgetId\") if isinstance(widget_id, str) and widget_id: sym = params.get(\"symbol\") tf = params.get(\"tf\") trade_ref = attrs.get(\"tradeRef\") or None trade_ref_type = attrs.get(\"tradeRefType\") or None # Degrade, never 500 the note write (same philosophy as the # rest of this function): an unrecognized tradeRefType is # dropped to NULL (the embed still saves, just as an # untyped/legacy-shaped reference) rather than blocking the # save. Note save is authoritative; this projection sync is not. if trade_ref_type is not None and not is_valid_trade_ref_type(trade_ref_type): trade_ref_type = None embeds.append({ \"widget_id\": widget_id, \"symbol\": sym.upper() if isinstance(sym, str) and sym else None, \"timeframe\": str(tf) if tf is not None else None, \"trade_ref\": trade_ref, \"trade_ref_type\": trade_ref_type if trade_ref else None, \"mode\": attrs.get(\"mode\") or None, \"captured_at\": attrs.get(\"capturedAt\") or None, }) if widget_id == _CHECKIN_WIDGET_ID: row = _checkin_row(attrs, params) if row is not None: checkins.append(row) elif widget_id == _BUILT_WIDGET_ID: use = _tool_use_row(params) if use is not None: tool_uses.append(use) elif widget_id in _TOOL_PARAM_KEY: use = _routine_tracker_use_row(widget_id, params) if use is not None: tool_uses.append(use) elif ntype == \"noteLink\": # Wave D. A note linking to the same target twice keeps BOTH # occurrences (position is part of the sidecar's primary key) -- # directive §64 wants the backlink UI to show one relationship # per SOURCE note, not one row per occurrence, and that de-dup # happens at the QUERY layer (get_note_backlinks), not here, so # this stays a faithful, ungrouped projection of what the # document actually contains. attrs = node.get(\"attrs\") target = attrs.get(\"noteId\") if isinstance(attrs, dict) else None if isinstance(target, str) and target: link_ids.append(target) elif ntype == \"financialFact\": # Wave F. attrs = node.get(\"attrs\") fid = attrs.get(\"factId\") if isinstance(attrs, dict) else None if isinstance(fid, str) and fid: fact_ids.append(fid) elif ntype == \"documentExcerpt\": # Wave J. Mirrors financialFact exactly. attrs = node.get(\"attrs\") eid = attrs.get(\"excerptId\") if isinstance(attrs, dict) else None if isinstance(eid, str) and eid: excerpt_ids.append(eid) # Same guard as the other walks in this file: _refuse_unbuildable keeps a # non-list content off every member write path, and this keeps a stored # body that predates it from 500ing the save. children = node.get(\"content\") if isinstance(children, list): # Plan A Task 2 (L-2): an internal note link MARK is a note link too. One # link bolded in the middle is several adjacent text nodes carrying the # same href -- it counts ONCE, so a run continuing the previous sibling's # href adds nothing. Any other sibling (plain words, a hard break) ends it. prev_href: str | None = None for child in children: href = walk(child) if href is not None and href != prev_href: link_ids.append(_internal_note_id(href)) prev_href = href return None if isinstance(body_json, dict): walk(body_json)
# j2_note_embeds -- delete+insert; document order (position) is the PK. conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM j2_note_embeds WHERE note_id = ?\", (note_id,)) if embeds: conn.executemany( \"INSERT INTO j2_note_embeds (note_id, user_id, position, widget_id,\" \" symbol, timeframe, trade_ref, trade_ref_type, mode, captured_at)\" \" VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)\", [(note_id, user_id, i, r[\"widget_id\"], r[\"symbol\"], r[\"timeframe\"], r[\"trade_ref\"], r[\"trade_ref_type\"], r[\"mode\"], r[\"captured_at\"]) for i, r in enumerate(embeds)])
# j2_note_checkins -- delete+insert, like the mentions below. The key is # (note_id, embed_id), and a copied block can carry its source's embedId: # the first in document order is kept, so a duplicate can never fail the # INSERT and with it the note write. conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM j2_note_checkins WHERE note_id = ?\", (note_id,)) if checkins: seen: set[str] = set() now = _now_iso() rows = [] for r in checkins: if r[\"embed_id\"] in seen: continue seen.add(r[\"embed_id\"]) rows.append((note_id, user_id, r[\"embed_id\"], r[\"day\"], r[\"mood\"], r[\"focus\"], now)) conn.executemany( \"INSERT INTO j2_note_checkins (note_id, user_id, embed_id, day, mood, focus,\" \" created_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)\", rows)
# j2_tool_uses -- delete+insert, like the check-ins above. One row per placed # widget, document order; readers count DISTINCT note_id, so a note holding one # widget twice is still one note. conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM j2_tool_uses WHERE note_id = ?\", (note_id,)) if tool_uses: conn.executemany( \"INSERT INTO j2_tool_uses (user_id, note_id, kind, tool_id, rev) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)\", [(user_id, note_id, kind, tool_id, rev) for kind, tool_id, rev in tool_uses])
# j2_note_mentions -- the one projection derived from body_plain, not # body_json; its own function so the body_plain backfill # (db.run_notebook_migration_v7) rebuilds it through this same code. _sync_note_mentions(conn, user_id, note_id, body_plain)
# j2_note_links -- a `noteLink` node's (or an internal link mark's, # Plan A Task 2) target id is NEVER validated # against j2_notes here: a link to a note that doesn't exist (foreign # tenant, already deleted, malformed id typed via direct API use) still # gets a sidecar row -- resolving whether that target is real, owned, # trashed, or purged is the READ path's job (get_note_backlinks / the # node view's own title lookup), which re-verifies ownership on every # call. Persisting an unresolvable row here is harmless (directive §33's # 'never silently delete source content' cuts the other way too -- this # sync must never REJECT a save because a link target looks wrong). conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM j2_note_links WHERE note_id = ?\", (note_id,)) if link_ids: conn.executemany( \"INSERT INTO j2_note_links (note_id, user_id, position, target_note_id)\" \" VALUES (?,?,?,?)\", [(note_id, user_id, i, tid) for i, tid in enumerate(link_ids)])
# j2_note_fact_refs -- facts are note-owned (Wave F checkpoint decision # 24): a factId this note no longer references simply drops out of the # sidecar; the owning j2_fact_observations row is untouched here # (removal-as-deletion is note_facts.delete_fact_observation's job, # called explicitly by the editor when a member removes a financialFact # node, never inferred from a save diff -- inferring it here would # delete a fact the member only temporarily cut mid-edit). conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM j2_note_fact_refs WHERE note_id = ?\", (note_id,)) if fact_ids: conn.executemany( \"INSERT INTO j2_note_fact_refs (note_id, user_id, position, fact_id)\" \" VALUES (?,?,?,?)\", [(note_id, user_id, i, fid) for i, fid in enumerate(fact_ids)])
# j2_note_excerpt_refs -- mirrors j2_note_fact_refs exactly. An # excerptId this note no longer references simply drops out of the # sidecar; the owning j2_note_excerpts row is untouched here # (removal-as-deletion is note_excerpts.delete_excerpt's job, an # explicit action never inferred from a save diff). conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM j2_note_excerpt_refs WHERE note_id = ?\", (note_id,)) if excerpt_ids: conn.executemany( \"INSERT INTO j2_note_excerpt_refs (note_id, user_id, position, excerpt_id)\" \" VALUES (?,?,?,?)\", [(note_id, user_id, i, eid) for i, eid in enumerate(excerpt_ids)])
# The task index (wave 10) -- refilled HERE because every door that writes a # body already calls this, in the same transaction, AFTER its body write. # ⛔ A document with no `taskItem` (the walk above saw every node) has no tasks, # so it pays no second walk: this function's one-walk claim holds for every # note without a checklist (test_sync_note_sidecars_walks_the_document_exactly_once). _sync_note_task_digest(conn, user_id, note_id, body_json if has_task[0] else None)
def _sync_note_task_digest( conn: sqlite3.Connection, user_id: str, note_id: str, body_json: dict[str, Any] | None, ) -> None: \"\"\"Refill one note's `j2_note_task_digest` row from the body just written: the tasks `note_tasks.extract_tasks` finds, or no row when there are none.
⛔ Must run AFTER the body write in the same transaction: the table's triggers (db.py) delete the row on every body write, so a refill written first is erased by the write that follows it. Correctness does not rest on this call -- a note with no row is computed from its body by `list_tasks` -- only the speed of the tasks view does.\"\"\" from api.services.journal_two.note_tasks import extract_tasks tasks = extract_tasks(body_json) if isinstance(body_json, dict) else [] if tasks: conn.execute( \"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO j2_note_task_digest (note_id, user_id, tasks_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\", (note_id, user_id, json.dumps(tasks))) else: conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM j2_note_task_digest WHERE note_id = ?\", (note_id,))
# ── Validation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _normalize_tag_path(tag: str) -> str: \"\"\"Nested tags (Obsidian's `a/b/c`): every level trimmed, empty levels dropped — so \"Research / Semis\", \"research//semis\" and a stray leading or trailing slash all name ONE place in the tag tree. A flat tag (no `/`) comes back exactly as `str.strip()` would give it: nothing else changes for the tags every member already has.\"\"\" t = tag.strip() if \"/\" not in t: return t return \"/\".join(seg.strip() for seg in t.split(\"/\") if seg.strip())
def tag_key(tag: Any) -> str: \"\"\"A tag's IDENTITY — the one key every comparison of two tags uses: the tag tree's node keys, its counts, the `tag=` filter (both halves), the search box's tag match and the bulk bar's add/remove.
Nested-path normalised, then lower-cased by PYTHON, which folds Unicode (\"Élan\" -> \"élan\"). ⛔ Never SQLite's `lower()` for this: it folds ASCII only, so \"Élan\" and \"élan\" were two tags to SQL and one to Python. ⛔ And never the STORED spelling: a tag saved before nested tags (\"Q3 / Q4\", the old validator only stripped it) is the same tag as \"Q3/Q4\" — the tree counted it under \"q3/q4\" while the filter compared the raw text and found nothing (review S2).\"\"\" if tag is None: return \"\" return _normalize_tag_path(str(tag)).lower()
def _sql_tag_match(value: Any, key: str) -> int: \"\"\"SQL `j2_tag_match(value, key)`: 1 when a stored tag IS `key` or sits below it (`key/…`) — a tag is the parent of its children (Obsidian).\"\"\" if value is None or not key: return 0 k = tag_key(value) return 1 if (k == key or k.startswith(key + \"/\")) else 0
def _sql_tag_is(value: Any, key: str) -> int: \"\"\"SQL `j2_tag_is(value, key)`: 1 when a stored tag IS `key` (no children).\"\"\" if value is None or not key: return 0 return 1 if tag_key(value) == key else 0
def register_note_sql_functions(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> sqlite3.Connection: \"\"\"Register the Python functions this module's SQL calls. Every connection that runs a `_notes_filter_sql` predicate MUST pass through here first — `no such function` otherwise. Deterministic, per-connection and idempotent; cheap enough to call on every read.\"\"\" conn.create_function(\"j2_tag_match\", 2, _sql_tag_match, deterministic=True) conn.create_function(\"j2_tag_is\", 2, _sql_tag_is, deterministic=True) return conn
def _tag_prefilter(key: str) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]: \"\"\"A cheap SUPERSET test on the raw `tags` JSON text, run before the per-tag Python match so a 50k-note library does not pay one Python call per tag per note. Sound WHATEVER THE WRITER, by construction: · a row that is pure ASCII (no byte above 0x7F) with no `\\\\u` escape is where SQLite's `lower()` and Python's agree, and JSON escaping is per character — so the JSON-escaped first segment of the key appears in `lower(tags)` whenever a stored tag's key matches; · every other row passes through to the exact check: one WITH an escape (`json.dumps`' default for a non-ASCII tag), AND one holding raw UTF-8 (`ensure_ascii=False`, SQLite's own JSON functions, an import) — `length(CAST(x AS BLOB))` counts bytes and `length(x)` characters, so the two differ exactly when a byte above 0x7F is there. ⚰️ Until fix round 3 only the escape passed, so soundness rested on an unwritten rule that every writer escapes: a raw-UTF-8 `[\"Élan\"]` was counted by the tree and NOT found by `tag=élan` (review R1-N1).\"\"\" first = key.split(\"/\", 1)[0] needle = json.dumps(first)[1:-1] return (\"(instr(lower(j2_notes.tags), ?) > 0 OR instr(j2_notes.tags, '\\\\u') > 0\" \" OR length(CAST(j2_notes.tags AS BLOB)) != length(j2_notes.tags))\", [needle])
def _symbol_note_ids_sql(user_id: str, symbols: list[str]) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]: \"\"\"`SELECT note_id ...` for the member's notes that carry a chart embed OR a cashtag mention of any of `symbols`: the ONE answer to \"which notes relate to this symbol\". The list filters (`ticker=`, `embed_symbol=`, the sector/theme `symbol_in`) and `get_symbol_backlinks` all read this one set.
⛔⛔ NON-CORRELATED, ON PURPOSE. This used to be two correlated `EXISTS (... WHERE e.note_id = j2_notes.id AND e.user_id = j2_notes.user_id AND e.symbol = ?)`. With no ANALYZE statistics (production runs none), the planner answered each EXISTS from `idx_j2_note_embeds_user_sym` `(user_id, symbol)` because it has two equality columns. That index holds EVERY embed of the symbol, so the check scanned all of them once PER NOTE. Measured at `acf1eb51e` (tools/notebook_scale_benchmark.py): `GET /notes? embed_symbol=` list+count took 717 ms p95 at 10k notes and ~14.8 s at 50k. As an `IN (subquery)` it is computed ONCE into an ephemeral index and each note is one probe.\"\"\" marks = \",\".join(\"?\" * len(symbols)) return (f\"SELECT note_id FROM j2_note_embeds WHERE user_id = ? AND symbol IN ({marks})\" f\" UNION SELECT note_id FROM j2_note_mentions WHERE user_id = ? AND symbol IN ({marks})\", [user_id, *symbols, user_id, *symbols])
class _RowidSets: \"\"\"One request's rowid sets, each computed ONCE and handed to every query of that request as a bound JSON array (wave 7, lane I).
`GET /notes` asks two questions over one filter set -- the page and its true total -- and each used to recompute the expensive part of the filter (the search's FTS + tag + ticker match, the tag filter's per-tag match) from scratch. Measured at 50k notes on a common search term: the match is ~42 ms and was paid twice. With this memo the page and the total read the SAME set, which also means they cannot disagree about which notes matched.
⛔ Only for queries on ONE connection within one request: the set is a snapshot of the moment it was computed. Keyed by the exact SQL and params, so two different sets can never be confused.\"\"\"
def __init__(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection): self._conn = conn self._memo: dict[tuple, str] = {} self._counts: dict[tuple, int] = {} self.computed = 0 # how many sets were actually run (rails read this)
def remember_count(self, where_sql: str, params: list[Any], n: int) -> None: \"\"\"Wave 10 (lane 10A): the relevance order already read EVERY row the filter admits (it has to, to order them), so `len` of that read IS the page's true total over that exact WHERE. `count_notes` then answers from here instead of scanning the library a second time. Keyed by the exact WHERE and params, like the sets.\"\"\" self._counts[(where_sql, tuple(params))] = int(n)
def known_count(self, where_sql: str, params: list[Any]) -> int | None: return self._counts.get((where_sql, tuple(params)))
def clause(self, set_sql: str, set_params: list[Any]) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]: key = (set_sql, tuple(set_params)) js = self._memo.get(key) if js is None: js = json.dumps([r[0] for r in self._conn.execute(set_sql, set_params)]) self._memo[key] = js self.computed += 1 return \"j2_notes.rowid IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))\", [js]
def prime(self, set_sql: str, set_params: list[Any], rowids) -> None: \"\"\"Record `set_sql`'s answer WITHOUT running it: `rowids` must be exactly the rows it returns, as a set (wave 10: the relevance order's one ranked MATCH pass already holds the text match, so the set and the total do not run the MATCH again). Counted as the one computation of that set.\"\"\" self._memo[(set_sql, tuple(set_params))] = json.dumps(sorted(rowids)) self.computed += 1
def _rowid_in(shared: _RowidSets | None, set_sql: str, set_params: list[Any]) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]: \"\"\"`j2_notes.rowid IN <set>`: inline as a subquery, or -- inside a request that shares its sets -- the set computed once (`_RowidSets`). ⛔ The SAME `set_sql` either way, so the shared form cannot drift from the inline one.\"\"\" if shared is None: return f\"j2_notes.rowid IN ({set_sql})\", list(set_params) return shared.clause(set_sql, set_params)
def _tag_clause(user_id: str, key: str, shared: _RowidSets | None = None, indexed: bool = False) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]: \"\"\"The note-carries-this-tag-or-one-below-it predicate, for a NON-EMPTY `tag_key`: the cheap prefilter, then the exact per-tag match. ⛔ ONE copy, used by the list/count predicate (`_notes_filter_sql`) and by the tag rename's roster (`tag_member_notes`) — a rename that found its notes by a different rule than the filter shows them would miss some, or touch others.
Wave 7 (lane I): phrased as a ROWID SET (`_tag_rowid_set_sql`), not a per-row test. See there for why.\"\"\" set_sql, set_params = _tag_rowid_set_sql(user_id, key, \"j2_tag_match\", indexed=indexed) return _rowid_in(shared, set_sql, set_params)
# Python's half of the tag index's `fold` (db.py): the SAME characters removed -- # imported, never retyped, so the two halves of the superset key cannot drift. _TAG_FOLD_TABLE = {code: None for code in j2_db._TAG_FOLD_REMOVED}
def _tag_fold(key: str) -> str: \"\"\"The tag index's `fold` of a `tag_key` (already lower-cased): every character `tag_key` may remove, removed (db.py `_TAG_FOLD_REMOVED`).\"\"\" return key.translate(_TAG_FOLD_TABLE)
def _tag_index_ready(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> bool: \"\"\"Whether `j2_note_tag_index` was BUILT on this database (db.py `_ensure_note_tag_index` records it in the build's own transaction). Until it is, every tag read takes the per-note scan: an index that exists but was never filled would answer from the notes written since, silently short. The record carries the derivation's VERSION (fix round 1, review I-3), so an index built by other code is not trusted either.\"\"\" return j2_db.schema_built(conn, j2_db._NOTE_TAG_INDEX_BUILD)
def _fts_map_ready(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> bool: \"\"\"Whether `j2_notes_fts_map.note_rowid` was made TRUE on this database (db.py `_upgrade_fts_map_note_rowid` records it in the upgrade's own transaction, and forgets it BEFORE any repair). Until it is, a search maps its matches through `note_id` -- the pre-wave-10 hop -- so a failed boot upgrade costs speed, never results (fix round 1, review I-2: a NULL `note_rowid` never satisfies `IN`, and the unguarded read answered `[]`).\"\"\" return j2_db.schema_built(conn, j2_db._FTS_MAP_BUILD)
def _tag_rowid_set_sql(user_id: str, key: str, match_fn: str, indexed: bool = False) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]: \"\"\"`SELECT rowid ...` of the member's notes (any status: the caller's own WHERE decides live / trash / archive) whose tags satisfy `match_fn(tag, key)` -- `j2_tag_match` (the tag or one below it) or `j2_tag_is` (exactly it).
⛔⛔ Wave 10 (`indexed`, when `_tag_index_ready`): from the tag index, never from the notes. An index seek on `fold` finds every ASCII text tag that CAN satisfy the match (an equal fold for `j2_tag_is`, a fold that starts with the key's for `j2_tag_match`); every other tag (fold NULL) is always read; and `match_fn`, the exact test, decides both. def _validate_tags(raw: Any) -> list[str]: if raw is None: return [] if not isinstance(raw, list): raise NoteValidationError(\"tags must be a list\") if len(raw) > MAX_TAGS: raise NoteValidationError(f\"tags exceeds cap of {MAX_TAGS}\") out: list[str] = [] seen: set[str] = set() for t in raw: if not isinstance(t, str): raise NoteValidationError(\"tag entries must be strings\") t2 = _normalize_tag_path(t) if not t2: continue if len(t2) > MAX_TAG_LENGTH: raise NoteValidationError(f\"tag exceeds {MAX_TAG_LENGTH} chars\") key = tag_key(t2) if key in seen: continue seen.add(key) out.append(t2) return out
def patched_tag_list(existing: Any, add: list[str], remove: list[str]) -> list[str] | None: \"\"\"Wave 6 (lane E) — a tag DELTA applied to a STORED list (`PATCH /notes/{id}/tags`): drop every tag whose identity (`tag_key`) is in `remove` — exactly that tag, a parent's children stay — then append each `add` the list does not already hold. → the new list, or None when nothing would change (so an idempotent request moves no revision). Pure: no SQL; the length and cap checks stay `_validate_tags`' (update_note runs it).\"\"\" before = list(existing or []) gone = {tag_key(t) for t in remove} out = [t for t in before if tag_key(t) not in gone] have = {tag_key(t) for t in out} for t in add: k = tag_key(t) if k and k not in have: out.append(t) have.add(k) return None if out == before else out
def renamed_tag_list(existing: Any, from_tag: str, to_tag: str) -> list[str] | None: \"\"\"Wave 6 (lane E, item 8) — rename `from_tag`, AND every tag below it, to `to_tag` in one note's list: `a` -> `x` makes `a/b` -> `x/b` (a tag is the parent of its `tag/…` children, as the tree and the `tag=` filter read it). Matched by identity (`tag_key`), whole levels only (\"researcher\" is not below \"research\"); a child keeps its OWN spelling below the renamed part. Two tags that become one are one (the first kept). → the new list, or None when nothing changes. Pure; a renamed child that outgrows the tag length is refused by `_validate_tags` when update_note writes it.\"\"\" before = list(existing or []) fk = tag_key(from_tag) depth = len(fk.split(\"/\")) out: list[str] = [] seen: set[str] = set() for t in before: k = tag_key(t) if k == fk: t2 = to_tag elif k.startswith(fk + \"/\"): t2 = \"/\".join([to_tag, *_normalize_tag_path(str(t)).split(\"/\")[depth:]]) else: t2 = t k2 = tag_key(t2) if k2 in seen: continue seen.add(k2) out.append(t2) return None if out == before else out
def _imported_widgets_private(body: Any) -> Any: \"\"\"Ruling R60 (privacy audit M-2): consent does not travel in a file. Every widgetEmbed in an IMPORTED body, at any depth, comes in with `params.share` False, so a note received from someone else (our JSON export, a connector, the confirm route) is never already shared and never publishes the member's own figures on the next See it now. In place; returns `body`.\"\"\" stack = [body] while stack: node = stack.pop() if isinstance(node, dict): if node.get(\"type\") == \"widgetEmbed\" and isinstance(node.get(\"attrs\"), dict): params = node[\"attrs\"].get(\"params\") if isinstance(params, dict): params[\"share\"] = False stack.extend(v for v in node.values() if isinstance(v, (dict, list))) elif isinstance(node, list): stack.extend(node) return body
def _validate_body_json(raw: Any) -> dict[str, Any]: if raw is None or raw == \"\": return {\"type\": \"doc\", \"content\": []} if isinstance(raw, str): try: raw = json.loads(raw) except (TypeError, ValueError): raise NoteValidationError(\"body_json must be valid JSON\") if not isinstance(raw, dict): raise NoteValidationError(\"body_json must be an object\") if raw.get(\"type\") != \"doc\": raise NoteValidationError(\"body_json must be a TipTap doc\") serialized = json.dumps(raw) if len(serialized.encode(\"utf-8\")) > MAX_BODY_JSON_BYTES: # ⛔ THIS STRING REACHES A MEMBER VERBATIM, TWICE OVER, BY DESIGN — # never re-word it at a display site. `NoteEditorPage`'s own # `friendlySaveError` deliberately shows a real backend detail # UNCHANGED (its own regression test: \"a real backend-authored # detail ... is preserved verbatim\"), and the import wizard's # \"Needs attention\" list renders `item.error` the same way # (commit.js). Measured 2026-09-21 against a real note that grew # past the cap while already open in the editor: the member saw # \"Save failed: body_json too large (>1MB)\" — an internal field # name, with no idea what to do about it. One raise site fixes # both surfaces; a per-surface translation would fix neither for # the other and would be a second authority over this sentence. raise NoteValidationError(TOO_LONG_BODY_DETAIL) # ⛔ Wave 10 (10C): never STORE a note no door can serve back -- see MAX_BODY_DEPTH. if _json_depth_exceeds(raw, MAX_BODY_DEPTH): raise NoteValidationError(TOO_DEEP_BODY_DETAIL) return raw

def _body_build_problem(doc: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None: \"\"\"Why the editor could not BUILD `doc`, or None when it can.
⛔⛔ WAVE 10, LANE 10C (OPEN-ITEMS \"POST accepts a body the editor cannot build\"). A body whose every TYPE is known can still be unbuildable: ProseMirror's `Node.fromJSON` throws on an EMPTY text node (\"Empty text nodes are not allowed\"), on a text node whose `text` is not a string, on `content` or `marks` that is present but not a list, and on a node that is not an object. The editor's content guard then LOCKS the note -- and until wave 10 told the member it held \"content from a newer version of the app\", which is false for a note that is merely malformed. Refusing it at the door means a note the editor cannot open is never CREATED.
⛔ Mirrors ProseMirror's own throws and nothing more: an unknown TYPE is not this check's business -- that is the newer-schema case the `X-UCT-Notebook-Schema` guard owns (`notebook_schema.check_body_write`). And it is ITERATIVE: a body may be nested deeper than Python's recursion limit.
⛔ Wave 10 10C fix round 1: ProseMirror's tests are JAVASCRIPT truthiness, so this reads them that way (`_js_truthy`). `content: {}` and `marks: {}` are falsy in Python and were skipped; in JS an object is truthy, is not an array, and throws. A node or mark with NO type (absent, null, \"\", a number, a bool, an object) throws too -- `schema.nodeType(undefined)` / `schema.marks[undefined]` -- and no bundle, older or newer, will ever register such a name, so it is malformed, not \"newer\". A LIST type is the one shape left alone: JS looks a property up by its string form, so `[\"paragraph\"]` builds, and `[\"text\"] == \"text\"` is true -- `_js_text_type` follows that rather than refusing a body the editor opens. \"\"\" top = doc.get(\"content\") if _js_truthy(top) and not isinstance(top, list): return \"the document's content is not a list\" stack: list[Any] = list(top) if isinstance(top, list) else [] while stack: node = stack.pop() if not isinstance(node, dict): return \"a node is not an object\" marks = node.get(\"marks\") if _js_truthy(marks): if not isinstance(marks, list): return \"a node's marks are not a list\" if any(not isinstance(m, dict) for m in marks): return \"a mark is not an object\" if any(_js_nameless(m.get(\"type\")) for m in marks): return \"a mark has no type\" t = node.get(\"type\") if _js_text_type(t): text = node.get(\"text\") if not isinstance(text, str): return \"a text node has no text\" if text == \"\": return \"a text node is empty\" continue if _js_nameless(t): return \"a node has no type\" content = node.get(\"content\") if _js_truthy(content): if not isinstance(content, list): return \"a node's content is not a list\" stack.extend(content) return None
def _js_truthy(v: Any) -> bool: \"\"\"JavaScript truthiness over a JSON value: null, false, 0 and \"\" are falsy; every object and every array -- EMPTY ones included -- is truthy.\"\"\" if v is None or v is False or v == \"\": return False if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool): return v != 0 return True
def _js_text_type(t: Any) -> bool: \"\"\"`t == \"text\"` with JavaScript's loose equality: a one-element array compares by its string form, so `[\"text\"]` (and `[[\"text\"]]`) is a text node there.\"\"\" while isinstance(t, list) and len(t) == 1: t = t[0] return t == \"text\"
def _js_nameless(t: Any) -> bool: \"\"\"True when `t` can never name a node or mark type: absent/null, \"\", a number, a bool or an object. A string is a NAME (an unknown one is the newer-schema case, not ours) and so is a list (JS looks it up by its string form).\"\"\" if isinstance(t, str): return t == \"\" return not isinstance(t, list)
def _refuse_unbuildable(body_json: dict[str, Any]) -> None: \"\"\"Raise the member-facing sentence when the editor could not build the body.\"\"\" if _body_build_problem(body_json) is not None: raise NoteValidationError(UNBUILDABLE_BODY_DETAIL)
def _extract_first_image(body_json: Any) -> str | None: \"\"\"The `src` of the FIRST picture in a TipTap doc (document order, depth first), else None. Cached to `first_image_url` so the notebook card can show a preview glyph without loading the whole body. Matches, in document order: - the standard '@tiptap/extension-image' node (type=='image', attrs.src) - a 'widgetEmbed' chart/widget node's captured snapshot (attrs.fallback.url) — so a note whose only content is a /chart still gets a thumbnail.\"\"\" def walk(nodes: Any) -> str | None: if not isinstance(nodes, list): return None for node in nodes: if not isinstance(node, dict): continue # attrs can be ANY shape on an imported/hand-crafted doc — a list # here crashed the whole note write (the `or {}` idiom only guards # None/falsy, not a truthy non-dict; inherited red's named fix). attrs = node.get(\"attrs\") attrs = attrs if isinstance(attrs, dict) else {} if node.get(\"type\") == \"image\": src = attrs.get(\"src\") if isinstance(src, str) and src: return src if node.get(\"type\") == \"widgetEmbed\": fb = attrs.get(\"fallback\") if isinstance(fb, dict) and isinstance(fb.get(\"url\"), str) and fb[\"url\"]: return fb[\"url\"] found = walk(node.get(\"content\")) if found: return found return None if not isinstance(body_json, dict): return None return walk(body_json.get(\"content\"))
def _validate_ticker(raw: Any) -> str | None: if raw is None or raw == \"\": return None if not isinstance(raw, str): raise NoteValidationError(\"ticker must be a string\") t = raw.strip().upper() if not t: return None if len(t) > MAX_TICKER_LENGTH: raise NoteValidationError(\"ticker too long\") if not re.match(r\"^[A-Z0-9.\\-]+$\", t): raise NoteValidationError(\"ticker has invalid characters\") return t

Public for the connectors' `.enex` adoption (Plan E Task 8), which compares a live title through this same rule.\"\"\" return (raw or \"Untitled\").strip()[:MAX_TITLE_CHARS]
def _import_payload_hash(note: dict) -> str: \"\"\"Compute a SHA256 hash of the note's immutable content for fingerprinting.\"\"\" basis = json.dumps({ \"title\": note.get(\"title\") or \"\", \"subtitle\": note.get(\"subtitle\") or None, \"bodyJson\": note.get(\"bodyJson\") or {}, \"tags\": sorted(note.get(\"tags\") or []), \"ticker\": note.get(\"ticker\") or None, \"folderPath\": note.get(\"folderPath\") or [], \"updatedAt\": note.get(\"updatedAt\") or \"\", }, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\")) return hashlib.sha256(basis.encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()
def _import_date(value, fallback): \"\"\"Validate and return an ISO date string, or fallback if invalid.\"\"\" if not value or not isinstance(value, str): return fallback try: datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace(\"Z\", \"+00:00\")) return value except ValueError: return fallback
def _body_has_import_placeholder(body_json: Any) -> bool: \"\"\"True when this body still carries an unresolved import-time MEDIA placeholder — `import-ref://<ref>` (an image/attachmentChip node whose media upload has not yet been confirmed). A raw substring scan of the serialized JSON, not a node-type walk: correct regardless of which node shape carries the placeholder, and cheap enough to run on every import_confirm write. False positive only if a note's OWN authored text happens to contain the literal string — harmless: it merely stays \"pending\" one write longer than strictly necessary, never loses data (see audit B5 / import_confirm's docstring).
Connector fidelity Plan A Task 4: MEDIA ONLY. An `import-link://<key>` mark used to count here too, so a link that could never resolve (a Notion page not shared with the integration) kept the note pending forever and `import_confirm` re-wrote it, and the engine re-downloaded its media, on every pass. \"Pending\" means something can still resolve by re-importing; a link is `_body_has_import_link`'s answer (`import_links_pending`), finished by the link heal pass (`note_connectors/link_keys.py`), never by a re-import.
Plan A Task 6: delegates to `import_notice.media_pending_state(...) == 1`, so \"retry now\" has ONE rule: a placeholder, or an importNotice with attempts left.\"\"\" return media_pending_state(body_json) == MEDIA_PENDING_RETRY
def _body_has_import_link(body_json: Any) -> bool: \"\"\"True when this body still carries an `import-link://<key>` mark — a cross-note link whose target is not here yet. The `import_links_pending` column is this answer about the STORED body, set by every import writer (`import_confirm`, the engine's `_apply_resolved_body`) and by `update_note`'s body write. Same substring scan as `_body_has_import_placeholder`, same harmless false positive.\"\"\" try: blob = json.dumps(body_json) except (TypeError, ValueError): return False return \"import-link://\" in blob
# Genuine resource bound on one import-check request — NOT a silent # data-hiding cap like the [:5000] slice this replaces (audit B1). That # slice truncated one note past the wave's own 5,000-note benchmark, and # the truncated tail came back \"not existing\" -> classified as a fresh # `create` -> a re-import of a >5,000-note library duplicated everything # past the cutoff instead of updating it, silently. SQLite's own variable # limit is handled below by chunking into groups of 500 regardless of the # total, so THIS cap exists only to bound one request's SQL round-trips # against a pathological payload (hundreds of thousands of keys). Set high # enough that a real personal library — the actual member this wave is # for — is always checked in full; a caller that somehow clears it is told # so honestly via `truncated`, rather than having its import silently # reclassify updates as duplicates. _IMPORT_CHECK_MAX_KEYS = 50_000
def import_check(user_id: str, import_keys: list[str], conn: sqlite3.Connection | None = None) -> dict: \"\"\"Check which import keys already exist for the user.
Returns: {\"existing\": {key: {\"id\", \"updatedAt\", \"importHash\"}}, \"checked\": int, \"total\": int, \"truncated\": bool} `truncated` is only ever True past `_IMPORT_CHECK_MAX_KEYS` keys in one request — chunking below (SQLite's own variable-count limit) checks every key up to that cap, never fewer. \"\"\" owned = conn is None conn = conn or get_connection() try: existing = {} keys = [k for k in (import_keys or []) if isinstance(k, str)] total = len(keys) truncated = total > _IMPORT_CHECK_MAX_KEYS if truncated: keys = keys[:_IMPORT_CHECK_MAX_KEYS] for i in range(0, len(keys), 500): # SQLite variable limit safety chunk = keys[i:i + 500] q = \",\".join(\"?\" * len(chunk)) # Wave 0 trash: a soft-deleted note's import_key must read as # \"doesn't exist\" here, not \"exists, needs updating\" — otherwise # a routine re-sync would silently resurrect content the member # deliberately trashed. `deleted_at IS NULL` is the same \"this # note is part of my active notebook\" predicate applied # everywhere else a note is looked up by identity. for row in conn.execute( f\"SELECT id, import_key, updated_at, import_hash FROM j2_notes \" f\"WHERE user_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL AND import_key IN ({q})\", (user_id, *chunk)): existing[row[\"import_key\"]] = { \"id\": row[\"id\"], \"updatedAt\": row[\"updated_at\"], \"importHash\": row[\"import_hash\"]} return {\"existing\": existing, \"checked\": len(keys), \"total\": total, \"truncated\": truncated} finally: if owned: conn.close()
def _newest_media_mtime(user_id: str, note_id: str) -> float | None: \"\"\"The newest mtime of any stored media file under the note's `inline/` and `file/` dirs (where `save_note_image_bytes` / `store_media` write), or None when there is none.\"\"\" newest = None for sub in (\"inline\", \"file\"): base = Path(_ATTACHMENT_ROOT) / user_id / \"notes\" / note_id / sub try: entries = list(base.rglob(\"*\")) except OSError: continue for p in entries: try: if p.is_file(): m = p.stat().st_mtime newest = m if newest is None or m > newest else newest except OSError: continue return newest
def _edited_since_file_import(conn: sqlite3.Connection, user_id: str, row: sqlite3.Row) -> bool: \"\"\"Plan B Task 10 (ruling R4): the file importer's \"hands off\" answer. The ONE predicate (`import_provenance.edited_since_import`) minus the legacy finalize shape -- a note whose only post-import write was the importer's own finalize PUT from before `update_note` stamped `imported_at` (`import_provenance.legacy_finalize_shape`). Never a second rule.\"\"\" updated_at, imported_at = row[\"updated_at\"], row[\"imported_at\"] if not import_provenance.edited_since_import(updated_at, imported_at): return False # Fix round 1 (ruling): the legacy shape describes only imports from before the stamp. if not import_provenance.predates_finalize_stamp(imported_at): return True later_version = any( import_provenance.is_later(v[0], imported_at) for v in conn.execute(\"SELECT created_at FROM j2_note_versions WHERE note_id = ?\", (row[\"id\"],))) return not import_provenance.legacy_finalize_shape( updated_at, imported_at, _newest_media_mtime(user_id, row[\"id\"]), later_version)
def import_confirm(user_id: str, payload: dict, conn: sqlite3.Connection | None = None, *, guard_edits: bool = False) -> dict: \"\"\"Transactional upsert of notes by fingerprint.
Plan B Task 10: `guard_edits=True` (the file-import route) never rewrites a note edited since its import (`_edited_since_file_import`): it is reported in `keptEdited` `{importKey, id}` instead. `payload[\"mode\"] == \"recover\"` (implies the guard) rebuilds every unedited existing note even when its hash matches and nothing is pending, keeping its folder and checkpointing the replaced content in version history; reported in `recovered` `{importKey, id, updatedAt}`. Any other mode is a `NoteValidationError`. The response carries `recovered` and `keptEdited` only under the guard, so the connector engine's call (no guard) keeps its exact shape and behaviour.
Payload shape: { \"source\": str, \"destFolderId\": str|None, \"notes\": [{importKey, title, subtitle?, bodyJson, tags, ticker?, createdAt?, updatedAt?, folderPath: [str, ...]}] }
Returns: {\"created\": [...], \"updated\": [...], \"skipped\": [...], \"failed\": [...]}
⛔⛔ audit B5: a fingerprint match alone does NOT mean `skipped` — a note whose body still carries an unresolved `import-ref://`/`import-link://` placeholder (`import_media_pending`, set here and cleared by `update_note`'s `importMediaPending` once the client's post-confirm media-upload + link-rewrite phase actually finishes clean) is written again and reported via `updated` instead, so a failed media upload gets retried on the member's next import attempt rather than silently and permanently missing its image forever. See `_body_has_import_placeholder`. Plan A Task 4: that flag is MEDIA only now; an `import-link://` mark sets `import_links_pending` instead (`_body_has_import_link`) and never defeats the skip -- the link heal pass (`note_connectors/link_keys.py`) finishes it.
⛔⛔ session-audit.md A1/A2: ONE note that cannot be stored (oversized body, malformed shape) is isolated to a per-note SAVEPOINT and reported in `failed` — it must never roll back its healthy siblings' writes in the same batch. Before this fix, ANY note raising here (most commonly `_validate_body_json`'s >1MB check, given the Obsidian ingest door used to accept markdown up to 5-7x that after conversion) caused a bare `conn.rollback(); raise`, discarding the WHOLE batch — measured against the real engine: a 200-note batch with one 1.2MB note landed as \"notes in the member's notebook: 0 of 200\", `status: ok`. This mirrors the export's own `EXPORT_ISSUES.txt` idiom (per-item try/except, name the failure, keep going) and the connectors engine's per-ref failure reporting (`fetch failed for {ref!r}: ...`) — the SAME convention, applied at the one call site that was still all-or-nothing. \"\"\" if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not isinstance(payload.get(\"notes\"), list): raise NoteValidationError(\"invalid import payload\") notes = payload[\"notes\"] if len(notes) > IMPORT_CONFIRM_MAX_NOTES: raise NoteValidationError(f\"too many notes in one batch (max {IMPORT_CONFIRM_MAX_NOTES})\") raw_source = payload.get(\"source\") if raw_source is not None and not isinstance(raw_source, str): raise NoteValidationError(\"source must be a string\") source = (raw_source or \"file\")[:40] mode = payload.get(\"mode\") if mode is not None and (not isinstance(mode, str) or mode != \"recover\"): raise NoteValidationError('mode must be \"recover\"') recover = mode == \"recover\" guard_edits = guard_edits or recover dest = payload.get(\"destFolderId\") or \"\" owned = conn is None conn = conn or get_connection() try: if dest: ok = conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM j2_note_folders WHERE id = ? Open chart REUSES a chart — one chart switches, several ask, none adds > ONE chart: it switches to NASDAQ:A50 at once — same widget, place, size, timeframe; no approval; Undo restores QQQ
Open chart REUSES a chart — one chart switches, several ask, none adds > ONE chart on a FULL board: the switch still succeeds (nothing to place)

routing — selection > nothing recognised → the FULL manifest (the pre-routing behaviour), never a guess

routing — selection > a recognised request gets its groups plus the always-on agent group, and names the rest
routing — selection > multi-intent requests select every group they touch
routing — selection > follow-ups keep the groups of a pending proposal and of the last change
routing — selection > a ticker in a symbol request routes to charts (case-sensitive on the raw text)
routing — selection > the kill switch sends the full manifest
routing — selection > a reroute ADDS the requested groups

a save as the last step of a plan > a local change runs at once with its own receipt; the save is then one card, on the board that change left
a save as the last step of a plan > Dismiss saves nothing; the change keeps its Undo
a save as the last step of a plan > a model plan proposed whole > one card names both; one Apply runs the change, then saves the board it left
a save as the last step of a plan > a model plan proposed whole > Dismiss runs neither
a save as the last step of a plan > a model plan proposed whole > saving into the open layout: approved on the card, it still asks again on the board the change left
a save as the last step of a plan > saved FIRST and then changed stays refused whole: the save would not hold what was asked
a save as the last step of a plan > a name already taken: the change still runs, and the member is told the save did not
a save as the last step of a plan > the dropped step is recorded as its own row, first; the rest still records as applied
a save as the last step of a plan > a fast-path request keeps one member row: the dropped step carries it, the rest does not repeat it
a save as the last step of a plan > a check that THROWS drops that step, in words and on the record; the rest of the request runs
a save as the last step of a plan > NEGATIVE: a step that can run records no partial row
a save as the last step of a plan > opening a layout and saving stays refused: the rest is itself exclusive
a save as the last step of a plan > saving into the open layout: its card comes after the change, so it is bound to the board it would save
a save as the last step of a plan > protected layouts > a chart change on an open protected layout refuses the whole plan: nothing changes, nothing is saved
a save as the last step of a plan > protected layouts > a save into a protected layout never runs, as a last step either

R-01 — normalizeArgs reads what the live planner sends (the browser half of turn.normalize_args) > screener.run: a sort-only refinement without filters, with a nested sort object, with "descending"

R-01 — normalizeArgs reads what the live planner sends (the browser half of turn.normalize_args) > never mutates the op it was given, and planOps applies the same tolerance on every path

R-01 — "turn the gradient off on this chart" is the dialog's own bgMode control > the model path with the live shape ({"key":"bgMode","value":"off"}): executed, not "couldn't fill in the details"

R-02 — an empty board: "add a daily chart of NVDA to this board" > the model path (the live plan: chart ops on the workspace entry, no chart on the board) = one new daily chart on NVDA, made at once — never "That target is not on the workspace"
R-02 — an empty board: "add a daily chart of NVDA to this board" > screenEmptyBoardChart: only an empty board, only chart symbol / timeframe / type ops on ONE target; anything else is left alone

R-03 — "rename Main Trading to x" is refused by name, before any path > through the panel: listed or not, the protected sentence — 0 model turns, nothing renamed

read awareness > compact context: own lists with ids/refs, sizes, symbols (the model may SEE a list; it is never the AUTHORITY for one), which one a widget shows; read-only flagged
read awareness > "what watchlists do I have" / "what's in Momentum" are answered from the real lists, no mutation
watchlist.add > ADD BATCH: all tickers checked, one write, receipt from the real list, one Undo removes exactly those
watchlist.add > DUPLICATE: never added twice; the receipt says what really happened
watchlist.add > INVALID ticker in a batch: nothing is added (all or nothing)
watchlist.add > TARGETING: a name resolves to the real list; "my watchlist" only when exactly one list is showing; else the model asks
watchlist.add > a list NAMED "… Watchlist" resolves on the fast path (show / add / remove / rename), with or without the word
watchlist.add > a big batch is proposed first; a linked list is read-only
watchlist.add > the list changed since the plan → refused at write time, nothing written
watchlist.add > STALE UNDO is delta-aware: other manual edits are kept; a removed Agent row blocks it
watchlist.remove > removes exactly the symbol; Undo restores it in its old place WITH its notes
watchlist.remove > Undo of a remove refuses once the list was edited (it would rewrite the order)
watchlist.remove > a symbol that is not there is said honestly
watchlist.create (+ populate) > ONE proposal, ONE transaction: created and filled; no workspace change; no member Undo
watchlist.create (+ populate) > an existing name (any case) is refused before anything is written
watchlist.create (+ populate) > if filling the new list fails, the new list is taken back — no mysterious empty list
rename, compound, compact-mode manifest > rename: proposed, by id, collision refused, Undo renames back
rename, compound, compact-mode manifest > two lists in one request (explicit: runs, no card), each list gets only its own symbols
rename, compound, compact-mode manifest > the manifest now carries >10 actions; watchlist args are closed schemas the server can check
rename, compound, compact-mode manifest > a saved-list proposal is NOT voided by a layout switch (it names the list, not the board)
failure honesty: a half-applied step is taken back, or said plainly > F1: add + rename on one list — the rename fails → the rows just added are removed; "nothing was left changed" is TRUE
failure honesty: a half-applied step is taken back, or said plainly > F1: if the take-back itself fails, the receipt says some changes could not be reversed
failure honesty: a half-applied step is taken back, or said plainly > F2: two new lists — the 2nd create fails → the 1st is taken back (no orphan list)
failure honesty: a half-applied step is taken back, or said plainly > F5: an Undo that fails part-way never rejects silently — it says what was and was not restored
context budget: explicit compaction, never a silent cut > many large lists: over budget the watchlist section keeps every list but fewer tickers per list, and says how many more
context budget: explicit compaction, never a silent cut > a normal library is sent in full (no compaction)

renders identity, timeframe bar and chart from props alone
density="compact" drops the meta row and the session toggle, keeps identity + timeframes
omitting onSymbolChange renders a static, non-interactive label
density="compact" fetches fundamentals with enabled=false (no fetch storm for a row it never renders)
density="full" (the /charts default) still fetches fundamentals with enabled=true
a pane showing the info row holds the snapshot for the rows ahead; compact and mini panes hold nothing
identityLabel renders the host label in the static slot and looks nothing up on sym
showTfBar={false} renders no timeframe bar at all
tfCodes overrides the user's favorites to render exactly those timeframes
with no onSymbolChange, a letter keydown on the chart surface is not intercepted

without tfCodes the overflow chevron is still there
density="mini" renders the timeframe bar and the chart, but no identity row, meta row, clock, or gear
density="mini" fetches fundamentals with enabled=false (it never renders the meta row that needs them)

onStore supplied (a /charts widget/tab) still renders the settings gear

/charts widget surface (stored + onStore): StockChart still receives the stored blob, workspace layout ignored
a popup with no chartsTheme prop follows the charts_theme pref
an explicit chartsTheme from the host still beats the pref

a /charts widget surface hands StockChart every look prop, from its own settings and the workspace theme

realtimeCandle registry — random tick / bar_close sequences > per-minute OHLC invariants + never moves back to an older minute — 400 seeds
barsStreamManager — random frame orderings > no consumer moves backwards; the last accepted frame of every bucket is delivered — 400 seeds

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-056 "could you flip the top-right one over to a weekly view": the scripted plan chart.setTimeframe on that cell; the cell and the saved grid read W; Undo puts D back; no other cell moves

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-056 (pre-model path) "make the top-right chart weekly": answered without the model; same read-back, same Undo, other cells untouched

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-057 "turn the bottom-left chart into plain bars": chart.setType on that cell; the cell draws bars; Undo restores its Style; no other cell moves

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-058 (D/W/M) "include extended hours on the top-left chart": chart.setSession; the cell's own session view goes extended; Undo puts regular back; the other cells stay regular

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-058 (intraday) "regular hours only on the top-left chart": chart.setSession writes the cell's own extendedHoursShading, saved; Undo drops it; no other cell forks

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-062 "alert me when the top-right chart goes above 250": alert.create on the NAMED cell's symbol (AMD, read from the grid), at 250, above; exactly one alert added; Undo leaves the book byte-identical; the grid is untouched

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-062 CONTROL: the member clicked the top-left cell (NVDA), the words name the top-right one (AMD): the alert is AMD's, none is NVDA's; Undo leaves the book byte-identical

Multi Chart execution family — rows an existing capability executes (PASS) > C3-062 CONTROL (the check has teeth): the same setup with a plan that alerts the ACTIVE cell's symbol is rejected by the same outcome check

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-042 "can you split my screen into a two by three grid of charts" from the BOARD: Multi Chart opens at 2×3; the four cells keep their charts, two new ones are empty; Undo puts the board back byte for byte

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-043 "I want three rows and four columns": a custom 3×4 grid (12 cells) through applyCustomLayout; Undo is exact
Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-043 a grid past the cap ("make it five rows by two") is refused in words; nothing changes

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-044 "close the multi chart view and take me back to my normal board": the grid leaves the screen, kept for next time; Undo brings it back exactly

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-045 "link the crosshairs across all four charts": crosshair sync on for the whole grid (the receipt says so); cells untouched; Undo is exact

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-046 "keep every chart scrolled to the same dates": time-range sync on (gridBoard reads it); Undo is exact
Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-047 "switch groups mode on": Groups mode on (gridBoard reads it); cells untouched; Undo is exact

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-048 "fill the grid with the space stocks": the picker's own fetch-and-fill — the ETF pinned first, the grid size kept, Groups mode on; Undo is exact

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-048 a group name that fits two groups ("the semiconductor group") is asked by name, never guessed; nothing changes

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-048 a group with nothing chartable: the picker would have switched Groups mode on first — the Agent takes that back, and nothing is left changed
Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-049 "go to the next group": Next › — the next theme's leaders fill the grid; Undo is exact

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-049 "switch over to the memory & HBM group" (an also-in chip): the switcher swaps the current group into the chips; Undo is exact

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-050 "refresh the group": ↻ Refresh — the loaded group re-ranked now; a cell whose ticker stays keeps its id; Undo is exact
Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-051 "get out of groups mode": Exit Groups — the group is dropped, the charts stay; Undo is exact

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-052 "open my Momentum Nine grid": the saved multichart grid (not the workspace layout of a similar name) replaces the board; Undo is exact

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-053 "save this grid as Chip Watch": one create-only POST of the menu's own shape (kind multichart, the cells, the member's scope); the grid is untouched; Undo deletes it
Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-054 BOUNDARY: a PREBUILT (global) grid is not the member's to delete — refused in words, no DELETE sent

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-055 "delete my Old Grid layout": shown first; Apply sends ONE DELETE of that row only; Undo saves it again under its name with its content

Multi Chart execution family — the grid itself (pl-grid: multiChart.set / multiChart.cell) > C3-059 "put the top-right chart back to my own chart settings": Reset to my chart — that cell drops its fork, keeps its Style pick and timeframe; no other cell moves; Undo is exact
